note: Topical subjects to decode into premium case studies — sourced for monetisation, engagement and reach. The case-study cycle drafts the top `queued` items (respecting each subject's `access`); the Operator's Daily Brief surfaces the queue every day. Keep it stocked: add subjects the radar/RSS and audience signals surface, retire drafted ones.

subjects.subject: MTN's pivot from connectivity to content — can a telco own African streaming distribution?
subjects.angle: The billing relationship + mobile-money rails as the most credible African-owned route into streaming.
subjects.rationale: High reach; extends the media-sovereignty thesis at brand level; strong monetisation lane.

subjects.subject: Checkers Sixty60 — how a grocery app became South Africa's most feared retail brand
subjects.angle: Retail-as-tech: owning the last mile and the customer relationship while rivals stumble (Pick n Pay).
subjects.rationale: Engagement magnet; a rare African-owned platform winning on execution + data.

subjects.subject: MaXhosa Africa (Laduma Ngxokolo) — knitwear heritage into an owned global house
subjects.angle: Owned-retail expansion vs licensing the aesthetic; the authorship-retention play, a companion to the Magugu dossier.
subjects.rationale: Pairs with the fashion dossier; strong African-authorship story.

subjects.subject: Flutterwave — the comeback bet and the IPO question
subjects.angle: Rebuilding trust and governance after turbulence; can it stay African-owned through a public listing?
subjects.rationale: High topicality; monetisation-relevant; companion to the Moniepoint dossier.

subjects.subject: The Springboks — building the world's most bankable rugby brand
subjects.angle: Converting back-to-back World Cups into a durable, monetisable national brand — who captures the value.
subjects.rationale: Reach + belonging; a national-brand authorship read.

subjects.subject: Nando's — the South African brand that quietly conquered the world
subjects.angle: African-authored global brand-building done right — humour, culture and ownership travelling intact.
subjects.rationale: Rare proof of African value-capture at global scale; evergreen engagement.

subjects.subject: Tyla — engineering a global African pop brand
subjects.angle: Grammy, 'Water', luxury deals — who owns the Tyla brand and how much value stays African.
subjects.rationale: Top-of-funnel reach magnet; keep public to pull audience toward the premium shelf.

subjects.subject: Jumia — the long turnaround and the African e-commerce thesis
subjects.angle: Path to profitability and whether pan-African e-commerce can be owned on the continent.
subjects.rationale: Investor-grade subject; monetisation and data-licence relevance.

subjects.subject: Cassper Nyovest's Billiato — celebrity spirits and the African drinks land-grab
subjects.angle: Artist-owned spirits vs multinational acquisition (Inverroche/Pernod) — companion to the Spearhead dossier.
subjects.rationale: Engagement + a bridge into the premium spirits dossier.

subjects.subject: Trace — owning the pipes of African music media
subjects.angle: A pan-African media brand built on the culture — how much of the value it actually owns.
